source: The Unlearning ladder (BRIEF §8): the advice everyone hears, sorted by whether it applies at your FOO step and where your banded ratios sit. Steps from data/foo_rules.json; zones from data/ratio_benchmarks.json.
confidenceNote: The mapping of advice to steps is a judgement, not a finding. It is here so it can be argued with line by line rather than baked into copy.
note: rules: each line names the advice, who says it, and when it applies — by FOO step (steps: [min, max]) and/or by a ratio's zone. Status is derived: applies / stop believing (you are past it) / not yet (you are before it) / unknown (nothing to judge by). No model call; every rule is a range. D-101.

rules.note: The first thing a deductible has to meet. After step 1 it is done, and 'save more cash first' becomes the thing to stop believing.

rules.advice: Pay off every debt before you invest a dollar.
rules.note: True of high-interest debt at step 3. Past it, a 4% mortgage is not an emergency and skipping the match to prepay it costs the match.

rules.advice: Always take the full employer match.
rules.note: A 50–100% instant return. Only 'not yet' while the starter fund is not there.

rules.advice: Keep six months of expenses in cash.
rules.note: Step 4's job. Before it, the starter fund and the match come first; after it, more cash is a choice, not a rule.

rules.advice: Cut the small stuff — the lattes, the subscriptions.
rules.note: Worth doing when the savings rate is out of band and there is nothing bigger to move. Otherwise it is the smallest lever in the room.

rules.advice: Max a Roth IRA every year.
rules.note: After the HSA and the full fund. Before that it competes with things that pay more.

rules.advice: Renting is throwing money away — buy.
rules.note: Only once the fund is full and a payment would sit inside the housing band. Before that it is a leveraged bet on one asset with no cushion.

rules.advice: Just buy the index and hold.
rules.note: From the match onward. It is not advice about whether to invest yet; that is the ladder's job.

rules.advice: Get a second job — you can't save your way out.
rules.note: Applies when the rate is out of band and the spending side has been looked at. Past it, hours have a price too — see Real Hourly Wage.
The target for the top of the ladder. Not a rule for someone still building the fund.
Always applies. It is the one line here with no 'not yet'.
Step 9: after every tax-advantaged dollar. Before that it is the lowest return on the list.
